page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a highly balanced profile with some specific bottlenecks. Multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls consistently in the average tier, as do Passmark CPU and database operations. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show a stark contrast: small-block cached reads perform at average speeds, whereas large-block uncached read and write operations are weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC processor cores and balanced resource allocation, the ecs.g6a.4xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring steady, non-burstable multi-threaded compute without the premium of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The lack of local storage and lower single-core performance make it less suitable for high-frequency trading or intensive local database caching. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, multi-threaded text and image processing, and standard application servers.
